course.title: Tiling
course.tagline: Lay floor and wall tiles straight, level and lasting.

days.title: Tiling Tools and Materials
days.goal: Know the tiling tools and materials.
steps: Lay out a tile cutter, notched trowel, spacers, level, sponge and bucket.
Learn the materials: tiles, adhesive (the glue), grout (the filler between tiles) and spacers.
A notched trowel is the flat tool with teeth that spreads adhesive evenly.
Set up a clean flat work area.
days.task: Label every tiling tool and material on your bench.
days.challenge: Name every tiling tool without looking.

quiz.q: What is tile adhesive?
options: The glue that sticks tiles to the floor or wall
quiz.explain: Adhesive is the glue that bonds tiles to the surface.

quiz.q: What is grout?
options: The paste that fills gaps between tiles
quiz.explain: Grout fills the joints between tiles and seals them.

quiz.q: What does a notched trowel do?
quiz.explain: The notches leave even ridges so tiles sit flat.

days.title: Plan a Tile Layout
days.goal: Plan where tiles go so cuts are even and the pattern is straight.
steps: Measure the floor and work out how many tiles you need.
Dry-lay tiles (lay them without glue) to check the pattern.
Plan so cut tiles at the edges are the same size both sides.
Mark the centre lines on the floor with chalk.
days.task: Draw a tile layout plan for a small floor.
days.challenge: Plan a floor so no cut tile is thinner than half a tile.

quiz.q: What is tile adhesive?
options: The glue that sticks tiles to the floor or wall
quiz.explain: Adhesive is the glue that bonds tiles to the surface.

quiz.q: What is grout?
options: The paste that fills gaps between tiles
quiz.explain: Grout fills the joints between tiles and seals them.

quiz.q: What does a notched trowel do?
quiz.explain: The notches leave even ridges so tiles sit flat.

days.title: Prepare the Surface
days.goal: Get a floor or wall clean, flat and ready for tiles.
steps: Remove old tiles, glue and dust.
Fill holes and level dips with levelling compound.
Check the surface is flat with a long level.
Prime dusty surfaces so adhesive sticks.
days.task: Prepare a small floor area ready for tiling.
days.challenge: Check a floor is flat enough to tile.

quiz.q: What is grout?
options: The paste that fills gaps between tiles
quiz.explain: Grout fills the joints between tiles and seals them.

quiz.q: What does a notched trowel do?
quiz.explain: The notches leave even ridges so tiles sit flat.

days.title: Cut Tiles Straight
days.goal: Cut tiles cleanly with a tile cutter.
steps: Mark the cut line on the tile with a pencil.
Score the tile once with the cutter wheel.
Snap the tile along the score line.
Smooth the cut edge with a rubbing stone.
days.task: Cut five tiles straight with no chips.
days.challenge: Cut a tile to an exact size first try.

quiz.q: Why dry-lay tiles before gluing?
options: To check the pattern and where cuts will fall
quiz.explain: Dry-laying shows the pattern and cut sizes before glue makes it permanent.

quiz.q: Why plan so edge cuts are even?
options: So the floor looks balanced, not lopsided
quiz.explain: Even cuts on both edges make the floor look planned and neat.

quiz.q: What should you do if a floor is not flat?
options: Level it first with levelling compound
quiz.explain: Tiles on a bumpy floor crack and sit unevenly.

days.title: Mix Adhesive
days.goal: Mix tile adhesive to the right thickness.
steps: Pour clean water in a bucket first, then add the powder.
Mix with a paddle until it is like thick peanut butter.
Let it rest for five minutes, then mix again.
Only mix as much as you can use in 30 minutes.
days.task: Mix a bucket of adhesive to the right thickness.
days.challenge: Mix adhesive that holds a ridge without slumping.

quiz.q: Why dry-lay tiles before gluing?
options: To check the pattern and where cuts will fall
quiz.explain: Dry-laying shows the pattern and cut sizes before glue makes it permanent.

quiz.q: Why plan so edge cuts are even?
options: So the floor looks balanced, not lopsided
quiz.explain: Even cuts on both edges make the floor look planned and neat.

quiz.q: What should you do if a floor is not flat?
options: Level it first with levelling compound
quiz.explain: Tiles on a bumpy floor crack and sit unevenly.

days.title: Spread Adhesive with a Notched Trowel
days.goal: Spread adhesive evenly so tiles stick flat.
steps: Scoop adhesive onto the floor with the flat side of the trowel.
Comb it with the notched side to make even ridges.
Hold the trowel at 45 degrees.
Spread only as much as you can tile in 15 minutes.
days.task: Spread adhesive in even ridges over one square metre.
days.challenge: Spread adhesive with ridges all the same height.

days.title: Project: Tile a Small Floor Area
days.goal: Tile a small floor area from layout to finished tiles.
steps: Dry-lay the tiles to check the pattern.
Spread adhesive and lay the tiles with spacers.

days.task: Finish a small tiled floor area, straight and level.
days.challenge: Lay tiles with no lips (edges sticking up) between them.

quiz.q: How do you cut a tile with a tile cutter?
options: Score once, then snap along the line
quiz.explain: One firm score and a snap gives a clean straight cut.

quiz.q: Why mix adhesive with water first in the bucket?
options: So the powder mixes evenly with no lumps
quiz.explain: Water first stops dry lumps forming in the mix.

quiz.q: How thick should mixed adhesive be?
quiz.explain: Thick adhesive holds ridges and supports the tile.

days.title: Tile Spacers and Straight Lines
days.goal: Use spacers to keep grout gaps even.
steps: Spacers are small plastic crosses that hold tiles apart.
Put spacers at every corner where tiles meet.
Check the lines stay straight with a long level.
Remove spacers before the adhesive sets hard.
days.task: Lay a row of tiles with perfectly even gaps.
days.challenge: Lay tiles so the grout lines are straight in both directions.

days.title: Check Tiles Are Level
days.goal: Check tiles as you lay them so the floor is flat.
steps: Press each tile down firmly and evenly.
Tap high tiles down gently with a rubber mallet.
Check with a level across two tiles at a time.
Lift and re-lay any tile that sits too high or low.

days.challenge: Find and fix a tile that sits too high.

days.title: Lay Floor Tiles Step by Step
days.goal: Lay a full floor of tiles in the right order.
steps: Start from the centre lines and work outward.
Lay full tiles first, then cut the edge tiles.
Keep checking level and straight lines.
Clean adhesive off tile faces as you go.
days.task: Lay a full small floor of tiles.
days.challenge: Lay a floor with no adhesive left on the tile faces.

quiz.q: Why hold the trowel at 45 degrees?
options: To make even ridges of the right height
quiz.explain: The angle controls the ridge height for even coverage.

quiz.q: How long can you leave spread adhesive before tiling?
options: About 15 minutes before it skins over
quiz.explain: Adhesive skins over quickly; spread only what you can tile fast.

quiz.q: What happens if you spread too much adhesive?
options: It dries before you lay the tiles
quiz.explain: Dried adhesive will not bond tiles properly.

days.title: Cut Tiles Around Pipes and Corners
days.goal: Cut tiles to fit around pipes, corners and door frames.
steps: Mark the pipe position on the tile.
Drill or nibble the hole with tile nippers.
Cut L-shapes for corners with two straight cuts.
Test the fit before you glue the tile down.

days.challenge: Cut an L-shaped tile that fits a corner exactly.

Clean all adhesive from the joints.

days.title: Clean Grout Haze
days.goal: Remove the cloudy haze grout leaves on tiles.
steps: Wait until the grout is firm, then wipe with a damp sponge.
Change the rinse water often.
Buff the tiles with a dry cloth.
Use a haze remover for stubborn cloudiness.
days.task: Clean a grouted area until the tiles shine.
days.challenge: Remove haze without scratching the tiles.

quiz.q: What tool pushes grout into joints?
quiz.explain: A grout float is a flat rubber tool that presses grout into joints.

quiz.q: Why wipe tiles with a damp sponge after grouting?
options: To remove grout from the tile faces before it hardens
quiz.explain: Grout left on faces hardens into a haze that is hard to remove.

quiz.q: What is grout haze?
options: The cloudy film grout leaves on tile faces
quiz.explain: Haze is the thin cloudy film left if grout is not wiped off.

days.title: Fix a Loose Tile

Lift the loose tile carefully.

Grout the joints again and leave to set.

quiz.q: What holds ceramic tiles to a wall?

quiz.q: Why press each tile firmly?
options: So the adhesive grips the tile fully

quiz.q: When can you grout a tiled wall?
